text:
Situation: Corvale East holds 10 units of the amino acid injection (500 mL) with 2.5 days of supply at current use. Corvale General holds 64 units (14.6 days). Corvale Lakeside holds 30 units (25.9 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA's drug shortage list does not include isoleucine, leucine, lysine acetate, methionine, phenylalanine, threonine, tryptophan, valine, cysteine hydrochloride, histidine, tyrosine, n-acetyl-tyrosine, alanine, arginine, proline, serine, glycine, aspartic acid, glutamic acid, and taurine as of 2026-10-21.

Our position: Internal redistribution can resolve the low supply at Corvale East without external purchase. Corvale Lakeside has sufficient stock to spare units while maintaining a two-week buffer.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 13 units of the 500 mL solution from Corvale Lakeside to Corvale East. Approval required: pharmacy director (transfer request).
2. If Option 1 cannot be executed, transfer 2 units of the 500 mL solution from Corvale General to Corvale East. Approval required: pharmacy director (transfer request).
3. If internal transfers are not feasible, initiate purchase from ICU Medical Inc. Approval required: buyer.

Not recommended: No external emergency procurement at this time; the product is not on FDA's shortage list and internal stock is adequate to cover the gap.
